title: test_ipv6_malformed_vector missing else clause for unknown expect_error values
description:
In python/tests/test_vectors.py lines 664-682, test_ipv6_malformed_vector handles specific expect_error values (packet_version, icmpv6_too_short, invalid_checksum, bad_type, bad_udp_length, invalid_source) but has no else clause or final assertion.

If a new expect_error value is added to ipv6_malformed.json vectors, the test would silently pass without exercising any code path.

Fix: Add an else clause with pytest.fail() or assert False to catch unhandled expect_error values.
close_reason: Added a fail-loud else (pytest.fail naming the vector and the unknown expect_error via !r) to test_ipv6_malformed_vector's dispatch chain (python/tests/test_vectors.py:720-721). ipv6_malformed.json contains exactly the six handled values (packet_version, icmpv6_too_short, invalid_checksum, bad_type, bad_udp_length, invalid_source — enumerated from the corpus), so the else only fires on future unknown/drifted values; it complements the existing _require_string_expect_error drift guard. test_vectors.py: 780 passed (rpl_messages + ipv6_malformed subsets green). ruff: only the pre-existing E501 at line 768 (present on HEAD, tracked by project-LICHEN-worker6-8dv7). 3x codereview via reviewer model (kimi-k3): correctness PASS, security PASS, edge-cases no findings.
